title: Kamlawati Devi v. State of U.P. & Ors.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Ashok Bhushan and Abhinava Upadhya, JJ.
disposition: Writ disposed; relegated to consumer forum or Supply Code objection.
headnote: Writ against a post-tenancy electricity demand was not entertained where a consumer complaint was already pending. The consumer was left to pursue that complaint or to file an objection under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Kamlawati Devi sought quashing of a 25 June 2012 demand of Rs 4,19,932. She said the Forest Department's commercial tenancy ended in 1995 with dues paid, that she was later billed commercially, that Complaint No. 66/2009 was pending before the District Consumer Forum, Basti, and that her 31 July 2012 Executive Engineer objection was undecided. The licensee said only domestic bills issued after 1995, that payments save Rs 2,500 were unproved, and that the connection stood in her deceased husband's name.

holding_units.holding: The Court declined to entertain a writ seeking quashing of a demand notice, holding it was not a fit case for writ proceedings. The petitioner having already filed a complaint before the District Consumer Forum, it was open to her to pursue that complaint or to file an objection in accordance with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ was disposed of on that observation.
holding_units.flag: Order cites the Supply Code 2005 generally; no clause numbered.

not_decided.point: Validity of the 25 June 2012 demand of Rs 4,19,932
Whether post-1995 billing was commercial or domestic, and the widow's liability on the deceased husband's connection
